dietEvidence.body: No skull or gut contents are known. Herbivory is inferred from related therizinosaurs with plant-processing dentitions and, in some cases, gastroliths; it is not a direct observation for Therizinosaurus.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A large therizinosaur known mainly from enormous manual claws and fragmentary postcranial material. Its diet is inferred as herbivorous, but the direct evidence is limited.
summary: A large therizinosaur known mainly from enormous manual claws and fragmentary postcranial material. Its diet is inferred as herbivorous, but the direct evidence is limited.

discovery.body: Named by Maleev, 1954. The record is known from the Nemegt Formation, Gobi Desert. The holotype, PIN 551-483, preserves fragmentary postcranial material and isolated manual unguals; no skull is known. Referred forelimb and hindlimb material has been described from the same formation.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, PIN 551-483, preserves fragmentary postcranial material and isolated manual unguals. Referred forelimb and hindlimb material has been described, but the hypodigm remains incomplete.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Nemegt Formation, Gobi Desert records the species in the Late Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈70–66 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The manual unguals are exceptionally large and curved. Referred forelimb and pelvic material indicates a bulky, short-legged body, but no skull is known.

behaviour.body: No direct evidence of behaviour. The enormous manual claws are preserved; their function in feeding, defence or display is unresolved. No nesting or social evidence is known.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from fragmentary postcranial material and isolated claws; no skull is known. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The holotype, PIN 551-483, preserves fragmentary postcranial material and isolated manual unguals; no skull is known. Herbivory is inferred from the wider therizinosaur record, not from this species’ jaws or gut contents. No integument is preserved.

primer.lead: Therizinosaurus cheloniformis was a huge therizinosaur from the [Late Cretaceous](/deep-time?period=cretaceous) of Mongolia. It is known mainly from enormous manual claws and fragmentary postcranial material; no skull has been found.
paragraphs: The claws are among the largest of any known animal. Referred forelimb and hindlimb material suggests a bulky, short-legged body, but the animal’s exact proportions are reconstructed from incomplete remains. Herbivory is inferred from the wider therizinosaur record, not from this species’ jaws or gut contents.

No feathers are preserved, so the presence of a covering is unknown. The function of the claws — feeding, defence or display — is unresolved. The dossier below is deliberately cautious about a dinosaur known from so little.
primer.takeaway: A giant therizinosaur known mostly from its claws, with no skull to tell us what it ate.
